question: Does the known native same-slot prefix-cache effect retain exact task quality and output parity, practical batch efficiency, and non-regressing tails on one new seeded 14B workload?
hypothesis: Same-slot prefix reuse preserves all observed exact answers and output token identities while reducing both service and full-attempt cost on this new 128-request key-copy population. Absolute service latency may still miss the frozen SLOs.
historical_evidence: The completed 2048-request historical 14B study informed this follow-up. It remains unchanged and was not protected confirmation. The stopped 0.5B branch remains closed with its confirmation unstarted.

model_runtime.thread_authorization: Explicit root exception to six-thread preference, within original owner-approved twelve-thread and one-heavy-job ceiling.
model_runtime.settings: Match historical 14B engine and sampling settings except new fixed seed, C4-only, two pairs and new producer archive. No additional setting change.

comparator: Identical model, actual prompt token IDs, offered requests, sampling and execution settings within pair. Baseline cache_prompt=false; candidate cache_prompt=true. No changed-input intervention or additional ablation.

cost_latency_gate.interpretation: Report joint exact-answer/latency goodput separately even if native quality/efficiency eligibility passes. No claim that practical relative gains imply acceptable absolute service latency. Shared setup/allocation costs retained without assigning them twice.

selection: One fixed unseen seed and scenario selected by root before generation or observation. No confirmation input creation before this freeze, no tuning, interim selection, additional seed/family search or replacement study.
isolation: Conventional prospective split: new fixed seed, frozen package/protocol before workload generation, candidate receives prompts only. Same Unix identity, accessible local files and no adversarial isolation; not cryptographically hidden data or external independent confirmation.
uncertainty: Exactly two balanced pairs; report both effects and minimum/median/maximum with per-request output transitions and nearest-rank p50/p95/p99. No IID-request, significance, population-risk or universal-gain claim.
stopping: Execute the one frozen study once. No retries. Stop on resource exhaustion, identity/protocol/runtime failure, cancellation, original deadline or 90-minute conservative queue-wrapper timeout. A failed/interrupted arm remains evidence; do not resume for a successful replacement.
claim_limits: Known cache mechanism and one held-out seed on one shared CPU host; no architecture or model-training contribution, controlled scaling law, external human validation, energy measurement or all-allocation savings ratio.
